findings.title: Total page count is off by one when membership is an exact multiple of the page size
findings.body: totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 unconditionally. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next control stays enabled, and navigating forward requests an offset beyond the data and displays an empty page. The count should use ceiling division (with the existing zero-count special case) rather than floor+1.

findings.title: Remove-member button appears for automatic groups because `automatic` is read from the member, not the group
findings.body: This template is rendered via {{each member in members itemView="group-member"}} in group.hbs, so its context is the member User object, which has no `automatic` property. {{#unless automatic}} is therefore always true and the remove (x) link is shown even for automatic groups, unlike the Add-members section in group.hbs which checks the group's flag correctly. Clicking it issues DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members for an automatic group, which the server rejects with 422, and Group.removeMember has no error handler, so the admin gets a dead control with silent failure.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client, silently losing the setting on new groups
findings.body: The group form always shows the alias-level combo box (even before a group has an id) and Discourse.Group#asJSON sends alias_level on POST /admin/groups, but create only assigns name and visible. A non-default alias level chosen while creating a group is silently discarded and the new group is persisted with the model default; update handles alias_level, create must do the same (or the control must be hidden until the group exists).

findings.title: members endpoint accepts unbounded, unvalidated limit/offset
findings.body: limit and offset are taken directly from params and passed to .limit/.offset. Any user who can see a group can request limit=1000000 to force the server to load and serialize the entire membership in one request (defeating the new pagination and enabling bulk scraping of member lists), and a negative limit raises a database error producing a 500. The parameters need clamping to a sane range (e.g. limit between 1 and the previous maximum) and offset to >= 0.

findings.title: Automatic-group remove_member test uses the wrong HTTP verb and cannot catch a routing break
findings.body: The test issues xhr :put, :remove_member while config/routes.rb only routes DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members to remove_member. Because controller specs dispatch directly to the action, the test passes regardless of the verb, so it gives false confidence that the endpoint the JS calls (DELETE, per Group.removeMember) is wired up. It should use :delete like the neighboring success-case test at line 125.

findings.title: findMembers no longer returns a promise when the group has no name
findings.body: Previously the empty-name branch returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([]); it now returns undefined. Any caller (including route hooks or future code) that chains .then() off findMembers() for a not-yet-named group - exactly the state of a newly created group object in the admin UI - will throw 'cannot read property then of undefined'. The branch should return a resolved promise to preserve the method's contract.
